items.title: Lew Soloff interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 16, 2000
items.q: But somebody around today that does that and does it with great emotion and has it all to me is Dave Liebman.

ctx.x: Improvising. Just enjoy the music. I think that’s it. I just enjoy the music. The other thing is, to me, to realize that when you’re playing with a rhythm section, stop thinking of yourself as a soloist and start thinking of the whole band as a group. And that way you don’t have to play every second. See it’s what you don’t play that’s also extremely important I think. In other words if the rhythm section is really grooving, you can play two notes, you can lay out for seven beats, or 14 beats, you can lay out,…

about time, really strong time, and they forget about melodic concept, horizontal concept. There’s a lot of people there that are thinking very vertically. Of course I could be biased, since it’s something I’ve never really taken to. You know since it’s not excited me that much I haven’t gravitated to it and try to learn it in great depth. So again, for educational purposes I’m saying it’s not sour grapes, because I can’t seem to force myself to get into that. It’s not my love. For somebody whose love it is, it’s…
Well said. It’s a great concept. One more thought I’d like to ask you —
